newsitem.title: USA: Flurry of earthquakes shakes San Francisco area.
newsitem.headline: Flurry of earthquakes shakes San Francisco area.

text.p: A flurry of four mild earthquakes shook the San Francisco area on Monday night, but there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.
Lu Page, a U.S. Geological Survey spokeswoman, said two quakes, each measuring 3.6 on the Richter scale, jolted the San Francisco area within the space of about four minutes.
They were interspersed with two lesser tremors, measuring in the 2.0 range on the Richter scale, the USGS said. The quakes were centered about 10 miles (16 kms) southwest of San Francisco, it said.
Page said she had heard no reports of injuries or damage. She said the tremors were believed to be on the unstable San Andreas Fault, one of the many faults that criss-cross California.
The two larger jolts could be clearly felt in San Francisco, where they set off car alarms in some streets.
Residents as far away as San Jose, 60 miles (95 kms) south of San Francisco, and San Rafael, 20 miles (32 kms) to the north, called San Francisco's KCBS radio station to report feeling the quakes.
